barRaise.topFinding: Nothing changed since the 2026-09-20 full pass: zero commits and a clean tree. All four hard-rule checks still pass and all sixteen open findings are MEDIUM. The one fix aimed at the duplicate-key bug still has not landed: the statement parser accepts a reference date, but the only production call site, apps/api/src/importers/index.ts:100, passes nothing, so a re-pasted statement resolves its year off the live clock. The privacy page still tells readers the source is published and auditable while GitHub reports the repository as private. That tension has now been seen five runs running, so this run makes the call: the repository stays private and the privacy sentence gets corrected.

docs/DECISIONS.md:7-29 D-016 rules the Plaid keep-or-delete question and its line 28 closes this id as decided. The repository-visibility wording the 2026-09-08 action row had drifted onto is not fixed; it stays open under security-05 and compliance-data-steward-02

The two mid-file imports are the half of this that is a defect, and they are gone: the import-pipeline import and the others now sit at the top of server.ts with the rest. The six-domain extraction is not done and is not closed with this: it is a structural refactor of a working file, it has no defect behind it, and the seven domains already extracted give the pattern whenever it is worth the churn. Recorded in BACKLOG.md rather than carried as an open finding, because a finding that means 'this could be tidier' re-raises for ever.

The quick-start command in scripts/README.md writes to X:\.secrets\YesAndBudget\scripts, which is where discord-notify.ps1 reads it from, and says plainly that a file left in the repository's scripts folder is never read. The four dead in-repository webhook paths are out of the ignore file, with a note saying why the three that remain stay: those are state the scripts genuinely do write beside themselves. Two script header comments that still named the in-repository paths were corrected.

Both step lists name every step. The release script's header gained the prose ratchet as step 0.5 and the usage-dashboard refresh as step 7, and scripts/README.md's quick-start list went from three entries to eight, which is what the release actually runs. Both say that a step added to the script belongs in both places.

sweepInterruptedImports moves every row still 'pending' to a new 'interrupted' status with a finished stamp and a message saying the process stopped. It runs at boot, before anything can create a new pending row, so the only rows it can touch are a previous run's. 'interrupted' rather than 'error' because nothing went wrong with the file. The status vocabulary in the shared package carries it and the import list draws it as a warning. Four tests in import-interrupted-sweep.test.ts pin the sweep against a real database, the message, the no-op case, and that the call sits before the server listens.

The relay capability key is out of the listing the web client reads. PlaidItemRow no longer carries relayKey, a new PlaidItemInternal extends it with the key, and items.ts exposes two listings: listItems for the HTTP route and listItemsInternal for the two server-side callers that unregister an item from the relay. The drain script reads the internal one. Typecheck and the 389-test suite pass, which is what proves nothing else was reading the key off a response.

The relay register route is rate limited per caller address, twenty new mappings per ten minutes, counted only when the registration creates a new mapping so a re-link of an existing item is never limited. A refused registration returns 429. The result also reaches the person now: ExchangeResult carries relayRegistered, and the connect flow raises a warning toast saying the account updates on a manual sync until the relay takes it, instead of the failure living only in a log line.

The privacy page no longer claims the source is published. The repository is private, which is what D-002 settled, and the page now says so along with the audit it can honestly offer: anyone running a copy has the whole source on their own machine. The launch checklist line that read as a done public repository was corrected to match. Making the repository public was the other option and was not taken: a session does not publish a private repository, and D-002 is a locked decision.

The staged-diff secret scanner's access-token pattern reads all three prefixes, sandbox joining production and development. A sandbox token is not a live credential, but it is the shape that gets pasted into a file during testing and then committed.

transactions carries categorized_by_rule_id, written by both rule passes, and findStaleCategorizations returns every row whose recorded rule no longer matches it or has been deleted, reachable at GET /api/rules/stale. A row with no recorded rule is deliberately not stale: that is a hand-set category or a row from before the column, and reporting either would bury the real ones. Editing a rule never revisited what it had already categorized, so the only way to find those rows was to remember which rule you had touched.

D-014 in docs/DECISIONS.md rules it: a project whose roadmap is complete reviews monthly, on the first Saturday, and rejoins the weekly rotation when it takes on new scope, meaning a new milestone or a new surface rather than a bug fix. The nightly canonical audit and the release gates are unchanged. The cadence follows the project's state rather than its bill, which is the same answer the cost number pointed at: a budget ceiling that skipped a run would make review coverage a function of the month's spend.

Closed as unrecoverable, not as fixed. This was reopened earlier on 2026-09-22 because a foreign project's queue row had closed it on a colliding finding identifier, which is not evidence. The reconstruction then failed: no bar-raise report in this repository carries an entry under this identifier, the ledger holds no prior evidence, and the title was overwritten by the reopening note, so nothing anywhere records what the finding said. There is no defect to verify and none to fix. Reopening it was right and leaving it open is not: an item nobody can read is not work, it is a row. The project's next review re-raises it with its own evidence if the underlying defect is still there, and the identifier collision that caused this is itself closed, since reconcile-status-queue.py now keys a close on the project as well as the finding.

parseByFormat takes a reference date and the import pipeline passes the import's own start, so every row in one import resolves a year-less date against the same instant rather than against the clock as each line is read. parseStatementText had accepted one since the 2026-09-15 fix and only its test ever passed one, which is what made the capability dead and left the dedupe key moving underneath a re-import. Three checks in import-reference-date.test.ts pin it: two references two years apart resolve a December line differently, two parses at the same reference agree, and the pipeline's call site carries the import's start. Typecheck and 392 tests pass.
